```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
                      fig.width = 8, fig.height = 5.3, dpi = 160)
library(ggplot2)
dir.create("figures", showWarnings = FALSE)
```

## Research question

How does maternal whole-blood **CXCR2 expression** vary with baseline vitamin D concentration and subsequent preeclampsia status? This exploratory project focuses on immune signaling. CXCR2 encodes a chemokine receptor involved in immune-cell signaling; its biological role motivates the choice, rather than a genome-wide search for significant results [1].

The continuous covariate is baseline 25-hydroxyvitamin D (ng/mL). The two categorical covariates are pregnancy outcome (normal pregnancy or preeclampsia) and vitamin D category (<30 or ≥30 ng/mL), derived from the continuous measurement. The cutoff follows the original study [2]; the labels describe study groups rather than universal diagnostic categories.

## Data source and preparation

The supplied GSE85307 files represent 157 participants in a nested case-control gene-expression study within VDAART: 110 normal pregnancies and 47 participants who subsequently developed preeclampsia [2,3]. These are whole-blood microarray expression measurements, not DNA genotypes. GEO documents RMA normalization on a log2 scale [4]. The supplied expression values are analyzed on their existing scale without another log transformation. The class file is a 500-probe subset, not the full transcriptome.

All preparation below occurs in R directly from unchanged copies of the supplied CSVs. The expression columns and covariate rows must be matched by sample identifier, not position.

```{r load-original-files}
covariates <- read.csv("data/GSE85307_covar-1.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
                       check.names = FALSE)
expression <- read.csv("data/GSE85307_geneExpression.csv", row.names = 1,
                       check.names = FALSE)
gene_names <- read.csv("data/GSE85307_geneNames.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# Stop rather than silently duplicating or losing participants.
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(covariates$geoID),
          !anyDuplicated(covariates$subjectID),
          !anyDuplicated(colnames(expression)),
          !anyDuplicated(rownames(expression)),
          setequal(covariates$geoID, colnames(expression)))
original_order_matches <- identical(covariates$geoID, colnames(expression))
expression <- expression[, match(covariates$geoID, colnames(expression)), drop = FALSE]
stopifnot(identical(colnames(expression), covariates$geoID))

# Use the provided linker, retaining probe identifiers as identifiers.
cxcr2_probe <- as.character(gene_names$PROBEID[gene_names$GENE == "CXCR2"])
stopifnot(length(cxcr2_probe) == 1L, cxcr2_probe %in% rownames(expression))

# Values are prefixed by descriptive strings such as '...: 22.4'.
strip_prefix <- function(x) trimws(sub("^[^:]*:", "", x))
vitamin_d <- as.numeric(strip_prefix(covariates$mat_vitD))
outcome <- strip_prefix(covariates$preg_preeclampsia)
stopifnot(all(is.finite(vitamin_d)),
          all(outcome %in% c("Normal", "Preeclampsia")))

analysis <- data.frame(
  geoID = covariates$geoID,
  CXCR2 = as.numeric(expression[cxcr2_probe, ]),
  vitamin_d = vitamin_d,
  outcome = factor(outcome, levels = c("Normal", "Preeclampsia"),
                   labels = c("Normal pregnancy", "Preeclampsia")),
  vitamin_d_group = factor(ifelse(vitamin_d < 30, "<30 ng/mL", "≥30 ng/mL"),
                           levels = c("<30 ng/mL", "≥30 ng/mL"))
)
stopifnot(all(complete.cases(analysis)), all(is.finite(analysis$CXCR2)))
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  Check = c("Initial participants", "Final participants", "Excluded participants",
            "Expression probes", "CXCR2 probe ID", "Original sample order matched"),
  Result = c(nrow(covariates), nrow(analysis), 0, nrow(expression),
             cxcr2_probe, original_order_matches)
), caption = "Data alignment and completeness checks.")
```

All `r nrow(analysis)` participants are retained. There are no missing values in the selected analysis variables. Values that appear unusual are retained because no documented measurement error has been established.

```{r group-counts}
group_counts <- as.data.frame(table(analysis$outcome, analysis$vitamin_d_group))
names(group_counts) <- c("Pregnancy outcome", "Vitamin D category", "Participants")
knitr::kable(group_counts, caption = "Numbers of participants in each plotted subgroup.")
```

## Plot styling

All three figures are made with ggplot2. The same categorical palette is used throughout; each figure is also saved as a PDF and a 300-dpi PNG. Captions distinguish descriptive patterns from causal conclusions.

```{r theme}
vitamin_colors <- c("<30 ng/mL" = "#0072B2", "≥30 ng/mL" = "#D55E00")
project_theme <- theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 15),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 11, color = "grey30"),
        legend.position = "bottom", plot.margin = margin(12, 16, 10, 10))
export_plot <- function(plot, name) {
  ggsave(file.path("figures", paste0(name, ".pdf")), plot,
         width = 8, height = 5.3, device = grDevices::cairo_pdf)
  ggsave(file.path("figures", paste0(name, ".png")), plot,
         width = 8, height = 5.3, dpi = 300)
}
```

## Figure 1 · Expression distribution

```{r histogram, fig.cap="Figure 1. Distribution of CXCR2 expression across 157 participants. Histogram bins have a width of 0.10 log2 expression units. No observations were excluded."}
histogram <- ggplot(analysis, aes(x = CXCR2)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.10, boundary = 0, fill = "#0072B2",
                 color = "white", linewidth = 0.4) +
  labs(title = "Distribution of CXCR2 expression",
       subtitle = "Maternal whole blood · 157 participants",
       x = "CXCR2 expression (log2 RMA signal)", y = "Number of participants") +
  project_theme
export_plot(histogram, "01_cxcr2_histogram")
knitr::include_graphics("figures/01_cxcr2_histogram.png")
```

CXCR2 expression ranges from `r sprintf("%.2f", min(analysis$CXCR2))` to `r sprintf("%.2f", max(analysis$CXCR2))` log2 units, with median `r sprintf("%.2f", median(analysis$CXCR2))` (Figure 1). The plot describes variation within this gene; it does not establish differences between clinical groups.

## Figure 2 · Vitamin D and expression

```{r scatterplot, fig.cap="Figure 2. Baseline vitamin D concentration and CXCR2 expression. Each point represents one participant. The line is an unadjusted ordinary least-squares fit; the shaded band is its 95% confidence interval for the mean response, not a prediction interval."}
scatterplot <- ggplot(analysis, aes(x = vitamin_d, y = CXCR2)) +
  geom_point(color = "#0072B2", size = 2, alpha = 0.65) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, color = "#222222",
              fill = "#9DA9B5", linewidth = 0.8) +
  labs(title = "CXCR2 expression and baseline vitamin D",
       subtitle = "Exploratory, unadjusted relationship",
       x = "Baseline 25-hydroxyvitamin D (ng/mL)",
       y = "CXCR2 expression (log2 RMA signal)") + project_theme
export_plot(scatterplot, "02_cxcr2_vitamin_d")
knitr::include_graphics("figures/02_cxcr2_vitamin_d.png")
```

The sample Pearson correlation is `r sprintf("%.2f", cor(analysis$vitamin_d, analysis$CXCR2))`, indicating a positive unadjusted linear relationship (Figure 2). This descriptive relationship does not show that vitamin D changes CXCR2 expression. Batch, cell composition, and other participant characteristics could contribute.

## Figure 3 · Expression by both categorical variables

```{r grouped-boxplot, fig.cap="Figure 3. CXCR2 expression by pregnancy outcome and baseline vitamin D category. Boxes show the interquartile range, with a median line; whiskers extend to the most extreme observations within 1.5 interquartile ranges. All individual observations are overlaid with horizontal jitter. Subgroup counts appear above the boxes. The preeclampsia/≥30 ng/mL group contains only six participants."}
counts <- aggregate(CXCR2 ~ outcome + vitamin_d_group, analysis, length)
counts$label <- paste0("n = ", counts$CXCR2)
counts$label_y <- max(analysis$CXCR2) + 0.10
boxplot <- ggplot(analysis, aes(x = outcome, y = CXCR2, fill = vitamin_d_group)) +
  geom_boxplot(position = position_dodge(width = 0.75), width = 0.6,
               outlier.shape = NA, alpha = 0.65, linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_point(aes(group = vitamin_d_group), shape = 21, size = 1.6,
              alpha = 0.65, stroke = 0.2,
              position = position_jitterdodge(jitter.width = 0.15,
                                            dodge.width = 0.75, seed = 103)) +
  geom_text(data = counts, aes(y = label_y, label = label, group = vitamin_d_group),
             position = position_dodge(width = 0.75), size = 3.5) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = vitamin_colors, drop = FALSE) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.04, 0.08))) +
  labs(title = "CXCR2 expression across pregnancy and vitamin D groups",
       subtitle = "All observations shown; subgroup sizes are unequal",
       x = NULL, y = "CXCR2 expression (log2 RMA signal)",
       fill = "Baseline vitamin D") + project_theme
export_plot(boxplot, "03_cxcr2_grouped_boxplot")
knitr::include_graphics("figures/03_cxcr2_grouped_boxplot.png")
```

```{r subgroup-medians}
medians <- aggregate(CXCR2 ~ outcome + vitamin_d_group, analysis, median)
knitr::kable(medians, digits = 3,
             col.names = c("Pregnancy outcome", "Vitamin D category", "Median CXCR2"),
             caption = "Descriptive subgroup medians supporting interpretation of Figure 3.")
```

Group distributions overlap (Figure 3). Differences in medians should be interpreted descriptively, particularly for the six participants with preeclampsia and vitamin D ≥30 ng/mL. These plots do not demonstrate independent effects or an interaction between pregnancy outcome and vitamin D.

## Interpretation and next steps

This first check-in describes one gene and the three required covariates. The sample is a selected pregnancy cohort, so its case fraction is not a population estimate of preeclampsia risk. Expression differences can also reflect blood-cell composition. The eight recorded microarray batches should be examined in any expanded analysis; the figures here are not batch-adjusted. No causal, diagnostic, or predictive claim is made.

For later submissions, CYP24A1 and PTX3 are biologically motivated additional genes available in the supplied data. An exploratory ten-gene clustering analysis could introduce unsupervised machine learning. Clinical labels would be withheld from the clustering inputs. This extension is planned, not performed in the first check-in.
